title: Prove isolated OpenBao Raft lab behavior and recovery
body:
## Goal / user outcome
Produce reproducible evidence whether a pinned OpenBao release is a viable future machine-secrets service, without making it a Fleet or production dependency. A three-node local container cluster is a functional Raft experiment only: because all nodes share host/power/kernel/storage failure, it MUST NOT be described as highly available.

## Current evidence / prerequisites
The repo has no OpenBao adapter or production service in the intake census (`note.md` §§32–50). Official OpenBao 2.7.x docs describe Raft replication/HA, leader behavior, Shamir per-node unseal, auto-seal lifecycle dependency, audit fail-closed behavior and KV v2 features. The dated addendum §7 requests three local synthetic nodes. No cluster, provider token, real data or live credentials have been used.

## Scope and boundaries
Create a disposable, pinned image-digest lab and scripts/config in an isolated, nonproduction location. Use synthetic fixture values only. Do not write production config, repo secrets, real account data, root keys or provider credentials. Do not add Fleet code/adapters, deploy to OCI/Kubernetes, change DNS/trust, or claim uptime. Record image/version, resource budget, host topology and exact commands.

## Experiment and acceptance
1. Start three Raft nodes with separate data volumes; verify membership, leader and quorum using OpenBao status/API. 2. Exercise successful synthetic KV read/write and policy-denied cross-path read/write. 3. Inject one process loss, restart, network partition, disk-full condition, full-host stop/start and audit-sink outage/hang. 4. Take a snapshot, restore to a clean isolated data directory/cluster, and compare a known synthetic manifest. 5. Record p50/p95/p99 for a bounded fixed workload, CPU/RAM/disk, recovery wall time, lost/duplicated operations and every manual intervention. Acceptance requires reproducible commands, pinned versions, all outcomes and a topology diagram; a whole-host outage MUST demonstrate that the same-host lab is unavailable. No production claim.

## Negative tests / oracle
Wrong token and insufficient policy must be denied; partition without quorum must fail writes rather than report success; corrupted snapshot must be rejected; absent audit sinks must show blocked or explicitly documented behavior; restored state must match fixture hashes/version metadata. Oracle: independent API read-back and hash comparison of synthetic fixtures, plus expected Raft quorum behavior; do not treat process health as data correctness.

## Recovery / rollback
Stop and remove only the disposable lab resources created by this issue. Preserve sanitized logs/config/metrics and snapshot checksums; destroy all synthetic secret values after evidence capture. Rollback is deleting lab artifacts, not changing any user service. Document recovery procedure and restore result.

## Dependencies / decisions
No blocking prerequisite. This is research, not deployment approval. Any V3 host, OCI, Kubernetes or production work requires a separate issue and human authorization. Unknowns: actual future host, desired RPO/RTO, budget, operator coverage and release target.

## Priority / size
Urgency 180 (future exploration; V1 work outranks it), importance medium, complexity very high; recommended V2. Evidence/source links: https://openbao.org/docs/configuration/storage/raft/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/concepts/ha/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/concepts/seal/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/concepts/recovery-mode/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/audit/ .

title: Map OpenBao secret, lease, Transit, PKI and SSH capabilities
body:
## Goal
Return a version-pinned capability matrix and go/no-go for each OpenBao surface independently; avoid adopting OpenBao wholesale or duplicating Fleet behavior.

## Current evidence
Current official docs describe KV v2 CAS/version/delete, leased dynamic secrets, Transit signing/encryption, PKI dynamic X.509 issuance and SSH certificate/OTP modes. Docs list ML-DSA-44 for Transit signing; this does not establish X.509 encoding, TLS KEX or ML-DSA OCSP support. Fleet currently has no OpenBao adapter (`note.md` §35).

## Scope
Use only FUT-01 disposable lab and synthetic values. Test KV v2, one selected dynamic engine, Transit Ed25519 and ML-DSA-44 sign/verify, PKI certificate/profile/CRL/OCSP behavior, and SSH certificate constraints. No Fleet implementation, production mounts, root key imports, real certificates or secrets. Pin exact server/API version.

## Acceptance / tests
For every capability record supported operations, API path, policy actions, version-specific limitations, payload limits, latency distribution, lifecycle and failure behavior. KV: CAS stale-write rejection and soft-delete/undelete/destroy permission separation. Dynamic engine: obtain, renew, revoke, expire and test downstream invalidation. Transit: independent verify, wrong-message/signature rejection, key rotation/version behavior. PKI: generated chain and profile constraints; check actual OCSP output and ML-DSA behavior rather than assuming. SSH: wrong principal/role must fail verification. Acceptance requires a table with evidence artifact per claim and explicit unsupported entries.

## Oracle / negative cases
Use independent crypto verifier for signatures/cert chains, API metadata for leases and version state, and policy-denial tests for unauthorized actions. Negative tests include stale CAS, expired/revoked lease, wrong key/message, expired cert, wrong EKU/issuer/principal, unsupported ML-DSA OCSP. Never describe a successful Transit signature as a PQ TLS handshake.

## Boundaries, recovery and rollback
No changes outside the disposable lab; preserve sanitized results only, then remove mounts and synthetic secrets. Rollback is lab teardown. Fleet remains owner of canonical credential IDs, cross-provider reconciliation and four-root policy; OpenBao may own only delegated service operation after separate decision.

## Priority / dependencies / unknowns
Depends FUT-01. Backlog; urgency 170, complexity high. Unknown exact adopted release, required production profiles, expected workload and whether any dynamic engine has sufficient supported plugin maturity. References: https://openbao.org/docs/secrets/kv/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/concepts/lease/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/secrets/transit/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/secrets/pki/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/secrets/ssh/ .

title: Compare OpenBao workload bootstrap and authentication methods
body:
## Goal
Determine whether a future nonproduction workload can authenticate to OpenBao with a short-lived, attributable identity and no baked-in long-lived bootstrap secret. Keep human SSO/OIDC ownership with #9077.

## Current evidence
OpenBao documents Kubernetes auth using ServiceAccount JWT/TokenReview and AppRole with constrained SecretIDs/response wrapping. SPIRE documents node/workload attestation and SVID delivery. No workload topology exists in the reviewed repo census; no integration was attempted.

## Scope
In a disposable synthetic environment, compare Kubernetes auth (including projected short-lived service-account token), JWT/OIDC validation, AppRole with response-wrapped pull SecretID, and TLS client certificate or SPIRE SVID integration only if available. No production identity provider, user account, SSO configuration, real secret, or reusable credential. Do not implement an OIDC issuer or absorb #9077.

## Acceptance
For each candidate: draw trust path and principal-to-policy mapping; document issuer/audience/namespace/service-account binding, token TTL/revocation semantics, bootstrap material, renewal, outage and compromise response. Demonstrate a valid workload gets one narrow synthetic path; a different namespace/service account/audience, expired token and revoked identity are denied. Show no static secret in image, repo, argv or environment artifact after login. Include a credential rotation and full bootstrap recovery test. Recommend no-go if identity is merely self-asserted or revocation is outside acceptable window.

## Oracle / negative tests
API policy read on only authorized synthetic path is positive oracle; cross-path and invalid-identity requests must return denied. Record exact auth method configuration and token expiry. Independent Kubernetes TokenReview or SPIRE Workload API evidence verifies identity provenance.

## Boundaries / rollback
Fleet owns mapping of verified workload principal to narrowly scoped grants; OpenBao owns auth role/policy; SPIRE owns attestation if chosen; #9077 owns human SSO/OIDC issuer/client lifecycle. Remove disposable role, tokens, service accounts and test artifacts after capture. No production rollout.

## Priority / dependency / unknowns
Depends FUT-01. Backlog, urgency 160, complexity high. Unknown future cluster, issuer, trust domain, service identity, and acceptable offline duration. Sources: https://openbao.org/docs/auth/kubernetes/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/auth/approle/ ; https://spiffe.io/docs/latest/spire-about/ ; #9077.

title: Prove OpenBao seal, audit and backup recovery paths
body:
## Deliverable
A tested recovery runbook and evidence set for snapshot restoration, sealing/unsealing, audit-device failure, and loss of auto-seal dependency in the disposable OpenBao lab.

## Current evidence / scope
OpenBao docs state Shamir threshold shares are required on each node after restart; auto-unseal depends on its external mechanism/key and recovery shares do not decrypt the data barrier; audit failures can block requests; recovery mode is an expert repair mechanism. No backup/restore of a deployed Fleet service has been performed. Use synthetic lab only. Never capture seal/recovery shares or root tokens in repository artifacts.

## Acceptance
1. Configure and exercise two audit destinations; stop each separately, then both; hang one to document request blocking. 2. Rotate log sink and confirm uninterrupted identifiable evidence; redact/HMAC synthetic payload according to configuration. 3. Snapshot and restore clean cluster with correct seal method; compare fixture inventory and policies. 4. Simulate unavailable auto-seal dependency, document whether startup/recovery succeeds and exact required external asset. 5. Measure RPO/RTO and hands-on steps. Recovery from snapshot must be demonstrated, not inferred from snapshot command success.

## Negative tests / oracle
No request should be claimed audited when both sinks are unavailable; no secret plaintext in logs; incomplete threshold cannot unseal; wrong snapshot/keys must not be silently accepted. Oracle: restored synthetic manifest, policy-denial tests and audit event IDs compared to expected request inventory; explicitly list unaudited system endpoints.

## Boundaries / rollback
Synthetic only; no production operator tokens, shares or provider credentials. Keep recovery material in ephemeral protected lab handling, not repo. Tear down test cluster after recording sanitized runbook. Rollback is lab teardown; never attempt recovery-mode mutation on any real cluster.

## Priority
Depends FUT-01. Backlog, urgency 155, complexity high. Open decision: Shamir vs auto-seal under future independent custodians/host. Sources: https://openbao.org/docs/concepts/seal/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/audit/ ; https://openbao.org/docs/concepts/recovery-mode/ .

title: Assess OCI Always Free feasibility for a nonproduction OpenBao site
body:
## Goal
Deliver a current, source-backed cost/resource/failure-domain decision on whether OCI Always Free can host a nonproduction OpenBao evaluation. This issue authorizes research only, not account signup, resource creation or deployment.

## Current evidence
Oracle's Free Tier docs currently describe a $300/30-day trial and Always Free resources after trial; A1 resources must total no more than 2 OCPU/12 GB across instances to avoid post-trial disable/delete. Home-region constraints apply. No user tenancy, quota, region or console was checked.

## Scope / acceptance
Use current official OCI docs and, only if separately available read-only, existing tenancy quota evidence. Produce itemized node RAM/CPU/disk, Raft quorum, block volume/backup, network/public-IP, bandwidth, monitoring, snapshot/restore, egress and monthly cost table with URL/date for every limit. Map each proposed node to actual independent failure domain (host, availability domain, region, account, identity control plane). Mark unknown if tenancy-specific capacity cannot be observed. Compare one small paid VM and basement lab at order-of-magnitude only, clearly labelled estimates. State outage and account suspension effects.

## Negative tests / oracle
Reject recommendation if three nodes exceed known free resource envelope, no independent failure domains, persistent data/backup is not viable, or hidden paid service is required. Oracle is published OCI allowance plus actual verified tenancy quota if available; never extrapolate free-tier from sales page to guaranteed capacity.

## Boundaries / rollback
No Terraform, CLI provisioning, billing changes, instance launch, token creation, public IP, or data upload. Research artifacts only; no rollback needed beyond removing draft calculations. Any deployment requires new approval and issue.

## Priority / dependencies
Depends on V2 resource results FUT-01 and recovery needs FUT-04. Backlog; urgency 100, complexity medium. Sources: https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/FreeTier/freetier.htm .

title: Validate Kubernetes secret and certificate delivery ownership
body:
## Goal
Establish which Kubernetes controller, if any, should own a workload's synthetic secret, certificate and trust bundle; prevent overlapping reconcilers and accidental data duplication.

## Current evidence
cert-manager documents certificate acquisition/renewal and CSI options; trust-manager distributes bundles; ESO syncs external stores into Kubernetes resources; Secrets Store CSI mounts external values. Current ESO support table marks OpenBao provider alpha, and CSI auto-rotation/sync features alpha. No Kubernetes cluster or provider has been deployed for this task.

## Scope
In a disposable cluster with synthetic values only, compare SOPS/age GitOps decryption, ESO OpenBao provider, Secrets Store CSI OpenBao provider, cert-manager for one test certificate and trust-manager for a test bundle. Pin versions. Do not connect BWS, 1Password, production OpenBao or use real age identities. Do not make multiple controllers target the same object.

## Acceptance
For each selected path document exact CRDs, RBAC, provider maturity, storage exposure (etcd/Kubernetes Secret/node filesystem), refresh interval, deletion semantics, pod reload/restart behavior, outage/stale behavior, rollback and upgrade support. Demonstrate rotation visible to consuming workload; revoked/removed access is denied or removed within stated measured bound. Demonstrate no competing writer by inspecting controller events and final owner references. Recommend a default only for tested path; otherwise no-go/defer.

## Negative tests / oracle
Wrong service account/policy denied; provider unavailable does not erase last known value unless explicitly configured; deletion cannot be misreported as provider outage; old certificate fails expected expiry/revocation policy. Oracle is synthetic source revision vs mounted/Secret value and controller status, plus negative API access.

## Boundaries / rollback
No production cluster or credentials. Delete disposable namespace/CRDs/chart after evidence; verify no test secrets remain. Fleet owns cross-store policy; OpenBao source; Kubernetes operators only delivery.

## Priority
Depends FUT-01/FUT-02. Backlog; urgency 105, complexity high. Sources: https://cert-manager.io/docs/ ; https://cert-manager.io/docs/trust/trust-manager/ ; https://external-secrets.io/latest/introduction/stability-support/ ; https://secrets-store-csi-driver.sigs.k8s.io/ .

title: Choose GitOps and infrastructure control-plane boundaries
body:
## Goal
Produce one decision record for prospective Cozystack/Talos management and tenant clusters specifying which system owns host config, GitOps reconciliation, CI and virtualization. Do not install any control plane.

## Evidence / scope
Backend dossier recommends evaluating Cozystack Flux/Helm vs Argo CD and clarifies Tekton is primarily pipelines/CI. Existing repo evidence does not verify a ready cluster, site topology or current Cozystack installation. Inventory current NixOS authority and existing CI only; no claims of deployed cluster without evidence.

## Acceptance
Compare Flux+Helm baseline and Argo CD on bootstrap, drift, RBAC/tenancy, dependency ordering, rollback, secrets decryption, cluster failure and upgrade burden. Place Tekton strictly in pipeline category and compare against existing CI rather than as equivalent GitOps tool. State one writer/source of truth per resource; map Fleet, NixOS, cluster operator, certificate controller and cloud IaC responsibilities. Include a failure-mode diagram and explicit no-go conditions.

## Tests / oracle
Use a table of concrete lifecycle scenarios (bootstrap, drift, operator outage, deleted resource, rollback) and verify documented behavior from first-party docs; a claim without primary-source citation is marked unverified. No cluster tests unless a separate disposable-lab issue authorizes.

## Boundaries / rollback
Documentation/design only: no repo config mutation, cluster access or deployment. No rollback required. Preserve NixOS host authority; mise is developer tooling, not host config.

## Priority / unknowns
Backlog, urgency 75, complexity medium-high. Unknown current infrastructure and operator capacity. Sources: https://github.com/cozystack/cozystack/blob/main/GENERAL_TECHNICAL_REVIEW.md ; https://fluxcd.io/ ; https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/ ; https://tekton.dev/ .

title: Determine whether attested workload identity or service mesh is warranted
stage: V2 synthetic lab; V3 only by approval
body:
## Goal
Decide whether SPIRE/SPIFFE and/or a service mesh adds a demonstrated workload-identity/security benefit for a defined Fleet service, or should be deferred. Do not install production mesh.

## Current evidence
SPIRE's official project docs describe node/workload attestation and SVID issuance. SPIFFE federation spec makes endpoint URL, profile and trust-domain binding explicit and directional. Tailscale identity-based connectivity is a separate access plane; membership does not itself authorize secret access. No workload topology or service-mesh need is verified.

## Experiment / acceptance
For a disposable two-service synthetic application, model static token baseline and compare SPIRE-issued X.509-SVID/JWT-SVID plus one candidate mesh only if needed. Define attestation inputs, SPIFFE ID, issuer/bundle trust, authorization mapping, rotation TTL, revocation bound, control-plane outage, bootstrap and multi-domain trust. Prove unrelated workload cannot obtain secret or impersonate other identity. Measure resource and operator burden. Decision must identify a concrete service and user outcome; otherwise recommend defer.

## Negative tests / oracle
Wrong node/workload selector, forged SPIFFE ID, wrong trust domain, stale bundle, expired SVID and compromised service identity denied. Oracle: verifier's identity assertion tied to attestation evidence, not workload self-claim; authorization policy separately denies unauthorized resource.

## Boundaries / rollback
No actual Tailscale/Teleport policy change, OIDC/SSO setup, production cluster, credential or public trust change. #9077 owns human SSO/OIDC; Fleet owns grant mapping; SPIRE owns attestation. Destroy synthetic cluster resources.

## Priority
Depends FUT-03/FUT-06; Backlog, urgency 85, complexity high. Sources: https://spiffe.io/docs/latest/spire-about/ ; https://spiffe.io/docs/latest/spiffe-specs/spiffe_federation/ ; https://tailscale.com/kb/ .

title: Model cross-provider reconciliation and lease invariants
body:
## Goal
Create a model-based test suite for eventual BWS/1Password/OpenBao coordination that exposes unsafe assumptions before implementing another provider writer.

## Current evidence
Specification §§20, 36 and backend dossier require three-way merge, explicit `zz.delete`, stable opaque logical IDs separate from native IDs, outage != deletion, scoped replication, immutable journal and no atomicity promise. OpenBao dynamic values have lease/renew/revoke lifecycle and are not KV replicas. For broker stale-value defect #6767, mitigation PR #8491 is merged; #6767 remains open pending deployment/canary, which is not authorized by this issue.

## Scope
Model two static provider replicas plus a lease provider, per-item allowed destination, source-of-truth, revision, tombstone and operation journal. Generate operation sequences containing concurrent edits, list timeout, unauthorized scope, provider partial write, retry, tombstone, lease expiry/revoke and stale cache. No live provider writes or credentials; use fake adapters and deterministic seed. Do not presume a common portable CAS operation: model conditional-write capability per adapter and expose race where absent.

## Acceptance and oracle
At least 10,000 generated sequences per test run or an equivalent documented property-test budget. Invariants: unavailable never becomes deleted; no unauthorized destination receives payload; conflicting edits never silently overwrite; dynamic lease value is never treated as indefinitely valid; retries are idempotent; opaque logical ID survives path/name/native-ID changes; partial completion is journaled and resumable; lack of provider CAS is never reported as serializable. Persist minimized counterexamples. Oracle is explicit model state vs system under test; no merely illustrative tests. Negative tests assert each invariant violation is rejected.

## Boundaries / rollback
No actual provider adapter, schema migration, broker deployment or canary. Place test only in owned test files after locating actual crate ownership; do not alter production providers. Standard git revert is safe for test-only code; retain failing counterexamples as fixtures.

## Dependencies / priority
No blockers; before any OpenBao bidirectional sync implementation. Backlog urgency 130, complexity high. Sources: spec §§20/36–38; addendum §8; OpenBao lease docs https://openbao.org/docs/concepts/lease/ ; issue #6767 and merged mitigation PR #8491.

title: Evaluate client-encrypted R2 continuity archive without deployment
body:
## Goal
Determine whether R2 can be a narrow offsite encrypted-artifact continuity sink, not a custom general-purpose credential service. No bucket, Worker or object is created.

## Current evidence
Cloudflare current R2 pricing lists finite free storage/operations and no egress charge; D1 read replicas are asynchronous and sessions provide sequential consistency; Secrets Store is limited and not readable back through API/dashboard. Existing dossier recommends client-side envelope encryption and separate key custody. No Cloudflare account or live pricing was checked.

## Scope / acceptance
Design and local synthetic proof of envelope format with authenticated encryption, unique object/version IDs, signed manifest, anti-replay/version monotonicity, optional immutable archive, key rotation, independent recovery key, and offline decrypt on a clean machine. Compare against SOPS/age artifact. Threat model object listing/read/write/delete, malicious service operator, key compromise, rollback, account loss and meter/billing limit. Include cost scenario from current official rates and sensitivity to excess usage. No Cloudflare API token or upload. Recommend no-go if it duplicates SOPS/age without meaningful independence or if no offsite restore owner exists.

## Negative tests / oracle
Bitflip, wrong key, swapped version, replay of old manifest, missing object, corrupted ciphertext and unavailable cloud must fail closed or restore the explicitly selected version. Oracle: independent decrypt/manifest verifier and expected plaintext hash for synthetic data; never claim cloud consistency from local proof.

## Boundaries / rollback
No root keys, real secrets, Worker/D1, IAM changes, billing changes or external writes. Remove local synthetic artifacts after report. Fleet owns archive manifest/policy if later adopted; R2 is bytes-only.

## Dependencies / priority
No prerequisite, but only pursue if actual independent continuity requirement remains after SOPS/age recovery. Backlog urgency 60, complexity very high. Sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/secrets-store/manage-secrets/ .

title: Define access-plane boundaries for Tailscale, Teleport and Cloudflare Access
body:
## Goal
Deliver a threat model and decision matrix for network/access products versus secret authorization, without changing a tailnet, Teleport deployment or Cloudflare Access policy.

## Current evidence
Specification §27.4/§46 and backend research distinguish connectivity/bastion from secret source. Tailscale documentation describes an identity-based connectivity platform; account tier and exact machine/workload identity requirements are not verified. #9077 owns SSO/OIDC.

## Acceptance
For each candidate map human principal, device identity, workload identity, network path, OpenBao/Fleet authorization, revocation, emergency access and audit evidence. Include a concrete sequence where authorized VPN access is insufficient for secret read and prove secret server independently denies unauthorized principal. Cite only current product-primary docs for feature claims; unknown commercial plan features remain unknown. Decision explains if any access plane solves an evidenced requirement; otherwise no-go/defer.

## Negative tests / oracle
Tailnet member with no OpenBao/Fleet policy must be denied; disabled user/device must lose path/access according to measured semantics; emergency operator cannot bypass audit silently. Oracle is explicit authorization decision and access log, not network reachability alone.

## Boundaries / rollback
Design only. No account signup, login, ACL edit, policy change, agent credential or external service call. #9077 owns SSO/OIDC, Fleet owns secret grants, access product owns connectivity. No rollback required.

## Priority
Backlog urgency 55, complexity high, depends only on an actual use case emerging. Sources: https://tailscale.com/kb/ ; https://goteleport.com/docs/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/ .

title: Compare SOPS/age, fnox and Fleet cache for offline continuity
stage: V2 synthetic evaluation (V1 behavior census only)
body:
## Goal
Determine the least-complex offline continuity approach for selected non-root synthetic credentials, keeping Fleet's API and current providers authoritative and avoiding a second cache that cannot invalidate.

## Current evidence
Repo census confirms SOPS/age use in NixOS but no Fleet-level provider abstraction. For broker stale-value defect #6767, mitigation PR #8491 is merged; #6767 remains OPEN pending deploy/canary, which is not authorized here. Addendum §3 prioritizes fnox evaluation; §4 requires age identity out of Git/Nix store. No fnox embedding stability or local benchmark is asserted.

## Scope / acceptance
Create reproducible synthetic fixture tests for SOPS/age decrypt on provisioned host, clean/cold host recovery, offline resolver, fnox CLI/library/daemon/cache if available, and current broker test harness. Measure cold/warm read, offline success, stale age, rotation invalidation, memory/disk plaintext exposure, subprocess overhead, and recovery steps. Keep root material excluded from ordinary resolver, hot-cache/prefetch, benchmark and equality-index paths; test only non-root synthetic credentials. Recommend one or no encrypted local artifact format.

## Negative tests / oracle
Wrong age identity and tampered ciphertext fail; provider outage returns unavailable not deleted; stale cache beyond configured max-age is denied for freshness-sensitive class; rotated synthetic value does not silently resolve old after invalidation; no unrequested secret values in argv/log/cache plaintext. The explicit `fleet secrets get` result is intentionally stdout; diagnostics/errors must be redacted. Oracle is expected fixture value/version and explicit clock/freshness model; test redaction scan over diagnostics and logs.

## Boundaries / rollback
V1 is the existing census only; this proposal adds no V1 implementation. No changes to production broker behavior, deployment/canary, or provider credentials. Test-only local files in temporary isolated directory; delete synthetic data. Any broker fix/deploy stays with #6767 and its owners.

## Priority
Backlog urgency 145 because continuity evidence matters, but do not block mandatory V1 features. Complexity medium-high. Sources: https://getsops.io/docs/ ; https://github.com/Mic92/sops-nix ; https://fnox.jdx.dev/ ; issue #6767 and merged mitigation PR #8491.
